subject: Logic
title: The Precautionary Principle
description: A quick, practical guide to The Precautionary Principle.

hook.text: A new chemical might be safe. The evidence is unclear. Should it be used while we figure it out?

buildup.text: The precautionary principle says: when the potential harm is severe, act cautiously even before proof.

discovery.text: It flips the burden: instead of proving danger, require proof of safety before proceeding.

twist.text: Critics say it blocks innovation. Everything carries some risk—taken to extremes, nothing would be approved.

climax.text: The key is proportionality: more caution for catastrophic risks, less for manageable ones.

punchline.text: When stakes are huge, caution isn't cowardice.

quiz.question: What does the precautionary principle prioritize?
options: Acting cautiously before proof of safety
